description: This repository is the main public collection of YANG modules, the data modelling language used to configure and monitor network equipment through NETCONF and RESTCONF. It is maintained by a community of committers around the IETF, with standards bodies and vendors contributing directly or as submodules. Coverage: standards-track and experimental IETF modules (drafts and RFCs), IEEE, ETSI, MEF, Broadband Forum and OpenDaylight modules, and vendor modules from Cisco, Juniper, Huawei, Nokia and others, organised by publisher, software release and platform. Together they describe interfaces, routing, transport, optical, access and device components as implemented or standardised. Format and access: YANG files in a public GitHub repository, with automated checks by GitHub Actions; free. Licence: set per directory: IETF Trust terms for IETF modules, Eclipse Public License for OpenDaylight, IEEE and Broadband Forum terms for theirs, and vendor terms for vendor modules; there is no single licence file. Caveats: the collection is very large, versions of the same module coexist, and a model says what equipment supports, not describing any network. Simulation uses: schemas for building network topology and configuration inputs for digital twin and capacity planning models of telecom networks. Related records: OpenConfig (data-openconfig-yang-models) is the operator-led model set in the same language, and the TM Forum Information Framework (data-tm-forum-information-framework-sid) covers the business layer above devices.
